subject: DPA clarifications and data handling follow-up (Acme Payments)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA clarifications and next steps (Acme Payments)

Hi Alex —

Great to meet you and the payments team this morning. Quick recap from my side and a set of asks so we can keep legal moving:

Call highlights:
- Primary use case: real-time transaction enrichment + merchant support macros (no credit card numbers stored; tokenized payloads).
- Expected volume: pilot ~500k requests/month, production ~5M/month.
- Residency preference: US (us-east) for PII; EU option for EU customers later.

Requested follow-ups you flagged:
1) Controller / Processor relationship in the DPA (we discussed Redwood as processor).
2) Subprocessor disclosures and the list of current subprocessors.
3) Breach notification timeline and escalation path (customer expects quick notice).
4) Data retention windows for logs and raw request payloads.
5) Evidence: SOC 2 report and any relevant architecture notes.

I've attached our latest DPA (DPA_Redwood_v1.2.pdf) and a short SOC2 readout. Can you confirm whether Acme will share redlines and which items are highest priority so we can loop in our legal team?

Next steps I propose:
- You share Acme redlines (if any) to legalops@acme-payments.com and cc me.
- If there are a small number of points (controller/processor, breach notice window, subprocessors) we can do a 30-min legal sync next week.

Thanks — I'll bring Dev and Rishi onto the thread for technical and legal coverage.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-payments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@acme-payments.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications and next steps (Acme Payments)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. A few quick clarifications from LegalOps so we can prioritize: 

1) Controller/Processor: Acme will be the Controller; we need Redwood to confirm it will be a Processor and accept standard processor obligations (data handling only for the purposes of the service).
2) Subprocessors: please provide a current list. We need to confirm whether any subprocessors operate in non-US jurisdictions (Acme policy requires disclosure).
3) Breach notice: Acme typically requests notification within 72 hours of discovery. Is that acceptable?
4) Data residency: for the pilot we need US-only residency for PII. Can you commit to hosting requests and storing PII in us-east region for this account?
5) Logging & retention: what's Redwood's default request/telemetry retention window and is there an option to shorten it?

LegalOps attached a redlined DPA for our initial pass (DPA_Redline-Acme.pdf). If you can respond to the bullets above and confirm who on your legal team owns DPA redlines, we'll decide whether to negotiate in DocuSign or via a short legal call.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Security & Compliance, Acme Payments
alex.johnson@acme-payments.com

Subject: Re: DPA clarifications and next steps (Acme Payments)

Alex — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. I pulled together responses below and included attachments (SOC2 readout + subprocessor summary).

Quick answers to your questions: 
1) Controller / Processor: Confirmed — Acme will be Controller, Redwood Inference will be Processor. We accept processor obligations in the DPA for processing only under documented instructions. We can sign the standard processor language in our DPA; our legal point is Rishi Malhotra (cc'd).

2) Subprocessors: Attached is our current subprocessor list (short-form) and locations. Key items:
- CloudProviderX (managed infra) — primary infra in us-east-1 (US).
- MonitoringProviderY — logs and metrics processing (US).
- Email/notifications provider — US.
We will provide the full subprocessors register and commit to 30-day advance notice of new subprocessors or immediate notice if critical.

3) Breach notice: Redwood's standard practice is initial notification within 72 hours of confirmed detection, with an interim timeline for preliminary info and a follow-up report within 30 days with remediation details. We can accept 72 hours as requested; if Acme requires a shorter SLA we can discuss exception language in the DPA.

4) Data residency: For the pilot we can pin Acme to our us-east region for data storage of PII and tokenized payloads. We'll document the region in the account config. Note: some telemetry and aggregated metrics are global for observability but do not include PII. If required we can escalate to a Dedicated/Private deployment for stricter isolation guarantees.

5) Logging & retention: Default request/log retention is 30 days for hosted accounts. Customers can request extended retention up to 1 year (for audit) or shorter retention if desired; Dedicated/Private deployments support customer-configured retention windows. We also offer a log export option to Acme-managed S3 on a scheduled basis.

Attachments included: SOC2-Readout-Redwood.pdf, Subprocessor_Summary_Redwood.csv (short-form).

Next steps:
- Rishi (cc) will review the redlines and propose language for the 72-hour breach notice and subprocessor disclosure clause.
- If it's easier, we can do a 30-minute legal sync next week — propose Tues 10–10:30 PT.
- I'll upload our signed DPA template to DocuSign once legal confirms final language.

Thanks — let me know if LegalOps wants to loop in any other stakeholders.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

Marissa — this is helpful, thank you. LegalOps reviewed and are broadly comfortable with Redwood as Processor and the 72-hour initial notification + 30-day follow-up. They asked two final items before we route for signature: 

1) Please confirm CloudProviderX is listed as operating in us-east-1 and that no primary processing occurs outside US for Acme account.
2) Can you confirm the mechanism for subprocessor notifications (email + posting to a customer portal or a subscription list)? Acme prefers automated notifications + a CSV register.

If you can confirm those two points we'll schedule the 30-min legal sync to close outstanding redlines and then route to DocuSign. Please cc Rishi and Dev on the confirmation so LegalOps has a single thread.

Thanks — Alex
